text:
oncall-bot: Incident alert: elevated 5xx on /v1/generate (hosted) — rolling 5m 5xx rate 2.3% (> SLO 1.0%). Paging primary oncall. Link: https://redwood.inc/incident/1887654321 :rotating_light:

ana: saw the alert, joining. I'm primary for this shift. quick check — is this limited to a region?

oncall-bot: Region: us-west-2, affected model: gpt-rlf-3b, pct of traffic: 28%. Error class: 5xx (backend connect errors, upstream timeout).

samir: I'm around — I can take secondary for this incident.

marta: adding context: we had a minor routing change an hour ago that bumped traffic onto the new dedicated pool. Could be related.

ana: good call. samir, can you pull the last 30m of envoy logs for the pool? I'll check the model-serving logs and KV cache metrics.

jonas: tagging runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/serving/backend-5xx. Steps 1-3 are the ones I usually follow (validate pool health, check GPU OOM, inspect kernel errors).

samir: pasting quick tail of envoy for the pool:
```
[2026-03-14T01:10:12Z] 10.0.5.12: upstream connect failed: connection reset
[2026-03-14T01:10:13Z] 10.0.5.13: upstream timeout after 15s
[2026-03-14T01:10:28Z] 10.0.5.14: upstream connect failed
```

ana: that aligns with time of deploy. I see a few kernels logging "kv_cache_eviction" and "rpc: handshake timeout" around 01:09-01:12. Could be overloaded CPU on control plane or bursty cache misses.

marta: are customers impacted? ops-manager asked earlier.

ana: initial impact: approx 6% of live sessions saw at least one 5xx on generation during the spike. Most customers self-retried and succeeded. No full region outage. I'll summarize for support.

ops-manager: please confirm if SLA breach is expected. If this is transient, we can avoid broad escalations.

samir: telemetry shows SLO window breached for 5m (above). We will hit automated escalation if not suppressed. Proposal: temporary SLO threshold raise to 1.8% for next 10m while we triage + fail traffic to fallback pool to drain bad instances.

jonas: hmm. raising SLO is sensitive. Could we instead suppress pager for the specific noisy alert rule and rely on error-volume alert to escalate if it grows? That keeps SLO reporting intact but avoids immediate page loops.

ana: preference is to suppress noise and do mitigation. Plan: 1) suppress 5m rolling SLO pager for /v1/generate in us-west-2 for 15m. 2) take the new dedicated pool out of rotation (route to fallback pool). 3) auto-drain bad hosts and redeploy kernel patch if needed. 4) postmortem if incident persists.

samir: I can run the commands. Using the incident-bot helper:
```
/incident suppress --rule slo_5xx_5m --scope region:us-west-2,endpoint:/v1/generate --duration 15m --reason "active mitigation - handoff"
/infra router set-weight --pool new-dedicated-pool --weight 0 --commit "temporary drain"
/infra pool health-check --pool new-dedicated-pool --wait 120s
```

marta: please include a note in the runbook thread about the suppress so subsequent oncall knows the state.

ana: executing suppression now. will also update the handoff notes for the next shift.

oncall-bot: Command accepted: suppression slo_5xx_5m for region:us-west-2,endpoint:/v1/generate until 2026-03-14T01:30:00Z by ana.

samir: router weight set to 0 and health-check started. 3 hosts returned unhealthy and are in draining state.

jonas: good. keep an eye on error rate and latency. If error volume drops but latency spikes >1000ms for p95, we should revert to smaller batch sizes or reduce concurrent streams for the pool. See runbook -> mitigations -> gradeload tweak.

ops-manager: a couple things I want logged for SRE review: rationale for suppression, expected customer impact, and explicit handoff notes for evening team. We're close to a handoff window.

ana: note added to thread and handoff doc: "Suppressed 5m SLO pager for us-west-2 /v1/generate until 01:30Z. Routed traffic off new-dedicated-pool due to upstream connect/timeouts. Expected customer-visible error fraction ~6% during spike; now decreasing. Contact: ana (primary), samir (secondary)."

marta: thumbs. Also recommend adding a short alert to #customer-success: "We had a transient error spike affecting small percent of generation requests in us-west; mitigation underway; we will post formal update after triage."

samir: error rate down to 0.9% in the last 3m post-drain. KV cache eviction errors still present but not majority.

ana: ok, I'm going to start preparing a short status note for support and schedule a follow-up in 30m. If anything regresses I'll re-open the suppression and escalate.

jonas: for the follow-up, let's capture: timeline, deploy diff (the routing commit), host-level logs for the 3 drained hosts, and whether kernel patch was applied.

ops-manager: thanks team. leaving this thread pinned to handoff notes. samir — you're secondary for the next shift; ana you'll add an explicit transition line in the oncall sheet before you sign out.

ana: will do. signing off in 20m, leaving detailed notes. If anyone pages after 01:30Z assume suppression will lapse unless extended.

oncall-bot: Reminder: suppression expires 2026-03-14T01:30:00Z. Auto-escalation will resume afterwards.

samir: acknowledged. I'll monitor and extend suppression if error creeps back up.

ana: thanks all. :white_check_mark:
